sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, and risk rises steeply as the share of the credit limit in use climbs, especially above about 0.7.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, with risk higher for applicants with at least one delinquency on file than for those with none.
The effect of utilization grows with the number of delinquencies: a high utilization adds much more risk for applicants who have past delinquencies than for those who have none.
Income has a weak to moderate effect, with higher income associated with lower default risk.
Length of credit history has a weak to moderate effect, with longer histories associated with lower default risk.
The debt-to-income ratio has a weak effect, and risk rises somewhat once the ratio passes about 0.44.
Age, number of dependents and months at the current address hardly matter, since the data do not resolve any clear effect for them.
The data do not settle whether the effect of credit history reverses direction with recent credit inquiries, so we do not draw a conclusion about that interaction.
